preserved_checks.subject: Main scope and hypotheses
preserved_checks.check: The theorem is read in its preceding fixed-family context: M is smooth Fano of dimension n+1; L is ample; positive integers d_i satisfy -K_M=(sum d_i)L; the F_i and F are sufficiently generic with smooth divisors and transverse intersections; 1<=m<=n-1. It does not assert hybrid convergence for every Calabi-Yau degeneration of the same skeleton dimension. The conclusion concerns normalized metric norms / potentials at the C^0 level, not metric-tensor, smooth or Gromov-Hausdorff convergence.
preserved_checks.outcome: No issue found in this scope check.

preserved_checks.subject: Deepest stratum, adjunction and dimension restriction
preserved_checks.check: There are m+1 divisors, so E_J has dimension (n+1)-(m+1)=n-m>=1. Adjunction gives K_EJ=(K_M+sum d_i L)|_EJ=0. The ample complete-intersection connectedness invoked in the text applies in this positive-dimensional range. Thus there is a single deepest connected stratum and one m-simplex with multiplicities one. This check also explains why the m=n boundary cannot simply be included: the deepest intersection is zero-dimensional and connectedness/constant-section surjectivity need not hold.
preserved_checks.outcome: The m<=n-1 restriction has a substantive algebraic role; no extension beyond that range was assumed.

preserved_checks.subject: dlt model and absence of a retraction assumption
preserved_checks.check: The specified local model is product(z_i)=t*y, with multiplicity one for the central components. The text explicitly flags that the preferred model is not Q-factorial and that a general dlt retraction is unavailable; it says retractions will not be used. The proof through Lemma 3.5 indeed uses values on the embedded skeleton followed by domination, not a purported global retraction. The general dlt classification of this local model remains a cited algebraic-geometric input; it was not proved from discrepancies here.
preserved_checks.outcome: No illicit retraction was found in the assigned proof range. Precise background terminology remains subject to the main agent's image review.

preserved_checks.subject: Valuation and hybrid scaling
preserved_checks.check: The constraint sum b_i x_i=1 correctly implements v(t)=1. At a nonzero complex parameter z, the displayed hybrid evaluation has logarithm log|f(z)|/|log|z||, matching the exponent 1/|log|t|| in Theorem 1.1. The t=0 evaluation e^{-ord_0(f)} agrees with the discrete valuation convention. This is a check of the formula and normalization, not an independent construction of the Berkovich analytification or proof of the fiber-identification theorem.
preserved_checks.outcome: No mismatch found in the hybrid rescaling used by the main result.

preserved_checks.subject: Top-dimensional volume normalization
preserved_checks.check: For a chart with all relevant a_i=0 and b_i=1, logarithmic radial coordinates range over an m-simplex of size |log|t||, giving the leading power |log|t||^m. In the hypersurface case the simplex {x_i>=0,sum x_i=1} has coordinate volume 1/m!, so the asserted probability density m! dx_1...dx_m is consistent. This verifies the leading scale and normalization in the actual reduced model. It does not independently establish every uniform O(1/|log|t||) assertion near exceptional or singular loci.
preserved_checks.outcome: No leading-normalization issue found; error estimates and the general weak-convergence theorem remain explicit dependencies.

preserved_checks.subject: Metric definitions and NA Calabi input
preserved_checks.check: For basepoint-free sections of kL the max expression transforms as a metric on L; division by k gives the correct change under a trivialization. Uniform limits define continuous semipositive metrics. The NA Calabi solution is unique only up to an additive potential constant, consistent with the suitable normalization in Theorem 1.1. In the application L is ample and the probability measure is supported on the finite skeleton/dual complex, matching the stated hypotheses of Theorem 2.7. A basis change in H^0(M,N0L) over C has trivially valued nonzero coefficients, so the preferred globally generated model metric is independent of the chosen basis.
preserved_checks.outcome: The application matches the theorem as stated. The cited NA existence, uniqueness and measure-continuity results were not independently reproved.

preserved_checks.subject: Quantifiers in varying-radius uniform approximation
preserved_checks.check: For each fixed approximant k one may first take |t|<r_k and then t->0. For two approximants j,k the normalized difference is bounded by epsilon_j+epsilon_k once |t| is below both radii; their NA limits are consequently a uniform Cauchy family. Thus the potential-limit argument does not require a common positive lower bound for r_k. The text also retains omega_h-psh on each fiber when invoking MA convergence. The passage of MA measures uses the cited Chern-Levine/Favre principle and is not established here solely from the elementary triangle inequality.
preserved_checks.outcome: No quantifier error found in the stated order of approximation and limiting operations.

preserved_checks.location: PDF 10 / printed 468; restriction maps preceding Lemma 3.1
preserved_checks.subject: Kodaira vanishing and section lifts
preserved_checks.check: For l>0, (l-sum d_i)L=K_M+lL, so the H^1 group in the hypersurface restriction sequence vanishes by Kodaira. The l=0 lift uses connectedness. Restriction to E_J can be checked successively along the smooth complete intersection: at each step the needed H^1 is of K_Y plus a positive ample multiple when either k>0 or divisors remain. At the final k=0 step the preceding Fano intersection has dimension n-m+1>=2, so Serre duality and Fano cohomology give the same vanishing; equivalently constants restrict isomorphically to connected E_J. Thus the chosen V_k complements are justified in this range.
preserved_checks.outcome: No missing positivity or connectedness assumption was found for these lifts.

preserved_checks.subject: Direct-sum decomposition and Hilbert series
preserved_checks.check: At the generic point of E_J the F_i form transverse regular parameters, and a nonzero element of V_k has nonzero residue. In a proposed finite relation, pass to the least total normal degree: distinct multi-indices give independent monomials over the function field of E_J, so the corresponding coefficient residues vanish, forcing those V_k coefficients to be zero. Iteration proves injectivity. The regular complete-intersection exact sequences yield P_EJ(y)=product(1-y^{d_i})P_M(y), giving the displayed dimension equality and surjectivity. Distinct exponents alone would not suffice without these nonzero residue and regular-sequence facts; both are supplied by the setup.
preserved_checks.outcome: Lemma 3.1's abbreviated argument has a valid completion under the stated hypotheses.

preserved_checks.subject: t-adic reduction and completion
preserved_checks.check: Every monomial divisible by product F_i can be replaced on X by -tF. Repeated replacement raises t-order by at least one and leaves the total L-degree fixed. After clearing one finite negative t power, all operations lie in a finite-rank R-module. R=C[[t]] is complete, so the corrections converge coefficientwise in Wtilde_l tensor R; dividing back by t^N gives the claimed K-valued lift. This uses formal completion, not analytic convergence in a complex punctured disk. The bounded-below integer a in (9) is consistent with this construction.
preserved_checks.outcome: No convergence gap found in the formal lifting step.

preserved_checks.subject: No cancellation, negative powers and boundary weights
preserved_checks.check: In the formal neighborhood of the generic point of E_J, F is a unit and t is product F_i times a unit. A term indexed by (l_0,...,l_m,a) therefore has leading normal exponent (l_0+a,...,l_m+a). Since min l_i=0, its minimum entry recovers a and then every l_i, proving injectivity of the exponent map. Coefficients have nonzero residue by the choice of V_k. Multiplying by a common t^N handles negative a. For strictly positive simplex weights higher-order unit terms cannot change the minimum; boundary values follow by continuity from the interior. Thus the check covers the closed skeleton rather than silently assuming positive coordinates throughout.
preserved_checks.outcome: No verified cancellation counterexample under the stated restrictions.

preserved_checks.subject: Finiteness, integer degree and global domination of the modified FS metric
preserved_checks.check: There are only finitely many tuples l_i>=0 with sum d_i l_i<=l, and for a fixed tuple only its least occurring a can maximize the expression, so (11) is a finite maximum. Put r=l-sum d_i l_i>=0. Multiplying the formula by N0 clears its displayed fractional degree: sections (product F_i^{N0*l_i}) tau_p^r have the integer degree N0*l, with weights N0(c_i-a). Hence it is an ordinary NA FS metric at a higher level. Global generation of N0L supplies a nonzero tau_p at every point. The old basepoint-free family and the valuation inequality ensure the new family has no common zero. For any model-regular coefficient section, its norm relative to the preferred model metric is at most one at every centered valuation; combined with the ultrametric inequality this proves phitilde_j>=phi_j globally.
preserved_checks.outcome: No fractional-degree, infinite-maximum or missing-global-inequality obstruction was found.

preserved_checks.subject: Direction and scope of the domination principle
preserved_checks.check: On the support of MA(phi_CY,0), which lies in Sk(X), the modified metric agrees with phi_j<=phi_CY,0. Both metrics are continuous semipositive, exactly as required by the invoked domination principle to extend phitilde_j<=phi_CY,0 globally. Combining this with phi_j<=phitilde_j and phi_j>=phi_CY,0-epsilon_j preserves the full global approximation error. The direction of the measure support and inequality is correct. This is conditional on the cited domination theorem, not an independent proof of it.
preserved_checks.outcome: The local-to-global step is consistent and does not assume a retraction.

preserved_checks.subject: Gradient constraint at the assigned stopping point
preserved_checks.check: Each slope of (11) in variables x_i=-log|F_i| is p_i=-l_i/l<=0, satisfies sum d_i p_i>=-1, and has at least one zero coordinate. These are precisely the stated union of faces Delta_k^vee. Positivity of the d_i bounds each p_i below by -1/d_i. Only this definition-to-slope correspondence was checked; the later Legendre representation and Proposition 3.8 are outside the assigned pages.
preserved_checks.outcome: No scope or sign mismatch found at the start of the dual-simplex construction.

Normalization check: on facet j, set y_i=-d_i p_i for i!=j. The integral of (1-sum y_i)^(n-m) over the standard m-simplex is (n-m)!/n!, and the Jacobian is 1/product_(i!=j)d_i. Summing over j yields C1=(sum_i d_i)(n-m)!/(n! product_i d_i), as printed.

PDF17-19 / pp.475-477: both transport measures have equal finite mass C1; dividing both by C1 reduces to probability measures without changing the optimal map. Tracked the almost-everywhere Jacobian equation, the lower bound on the weighted Alexandrov measure, and equality from the total-mass bound.

PDF18-19 / pp.476-477: the subgradient graph is closed and the target facet boundaries have zero target measure. After excluding the Lebesgue-null nondifferentiability set, the weighted MA equation makes the wall set null. Connectedness of a subgradient set in the quotient prevents it from lying in two disjoint cell interiors without meeting a wall, giving the full-measure chamber union.

PDF19-20 / pp.477-478: tracked the cited regularity hypotheses: convex target, locally doubling source and polynomial-weight target densities, local positivity of W, and its Lipschitz regularity. On each chamber W is analytic. The compact-set gap to the other target cells in Lemma4.8 persists on a neighborhood, so p_k=0 makes the canonical extension independent of x_k there; shrinking that neighborhood transfers the chamber smoothness.

PDF20-22 / pp.478-480: checked semipositivity of both ansatz constructions. The inequalities p_i<=0 and 1+sum_i d_i p_i>=0 give positive curvature coefficients. Clearing denominators by k*N0 in (21) produces genuine sections of one line-bundle power; the p=0 terms supply a basepoint-free family.

Uniform grid approximation: choose q_i=ceil(k p_i)/k. Then q remains in Delta-dual, q_i>=p_i, and |q-p|<=C/k. For the NA coordinates -log|F_i|>=0, the linear pairing can only improve on replacing p by q, so the Lipschitz error of u* is O(1/k), even near a divisor. In the complex setting x_i>=-C/|log|t||, giving the extra bounded error and the printed C(1+k^(-1)|log|t||) estimate.

PDF22-24 / pp.480-482: checked the rank-m normal Hessian term, the binomial coefficient n!/[m!(n-m)!], and the m! determinant factor in (24). Equation(19) cancels W=(1+sum d_i u_i)^(n-m); equation(22) then cancels the product of d_i and the remaining m!, leaving (sum d_i)(L^(n+1).M) mu_t=(L^n)mu_t.

The generic-region approximations are made only after selecting compact subsets of chambers, so Hessian bounds, a positive lower bound on W, and positive normal Hessian eigenvalues are available with constants depending on delta. The small coefficient 1/|log|t|| controls cross terms, while exponentially small normal coordinates suppress terms with additional ambient factors.

Combining this with hybrid convergence of mu_t and Corollary5.5 identifies the NA MA measure; the resulting CY metric identification uses the earlier uniqueness statement, with its additive normalization.

PDF25-26 / pp.483-484: checked the normalization in the stability application: omega=omega_CY,t/|log|t||, phi=-psi_t, and normalized omega^n=mu_t. The contradiction hypothesis supplies the sublevel mass for a=-delta, b=delta; choose gamma small enough that C*gamma<delta/2 and then t small enough for the TV requirement. The order of choices is legitimate even though C depends on delta: delta is fixed before t tends to0.

preserved_checks.claim: Uniform smallness of psi_t on the generic logarithmic region.
check: Set v=phi/|log|t||-u(y), where phi=phi_h+phi_t+|log|t||psi_t. Equation(27), bounded phi_h, and psi_t>=0 give v>=-C epsilon on the local region for t sufficiently small.

Choose the exceptional-measure threshold delta<=epsilon^(m+1). The uniform L-infinity bound on psi_t bounds its exceptional-set contribution by O(epsilon^(m+1)); the ordinary part has oscillation O(epsilon) on a logarithmic ball of volume O(epsilon^m).
After averaging the compact directions and torus angles, the normalized local L1 bound is O(epsilon). Convexity in the logarithmic radii gives an interior upper bound after shrinking.

Applying the psh submean estimate to the nonnegative function v+C epsilon transfers the upper bound from its angular/local average to v. This uses the stronger lower bound after subtracting u(y), which follows directly from equation(27); it does not require u(y)=0.
Subtracting phi_t/|log|t|| and phi_h/|log|t|| then yields psi_t<=C epsilon.

preserved_checks.claim: A point-normalized section with a weighted L2 estimate uniform for small t and large l.
check: The fixed N0 background contribution gives a curvature lower bound independent of l, while the remaining l-N0 weight uses the positive CY metric.
The chosen section is normalized at the specified z. The cost from the Jacobian/volume ratio is exponential in |log|t||, hence contributes O(|log|t||/l) after taking the logarithm divided by2l.
The passage from the l-N0 weight to the l weight costs at most exp(C|log|t||) because the potential is uniformly O(|log|t||). This keeps the final constant independent of l.
preserved_checks.boundary: The external Ohsawa–Takegoshi theorem, its precise singular-zero-set applicability, and the uniform algebraic lower bound for the selected Jacobian were read as stated dependencies; they were not independently reconstructed from the cited monograph.

preserved_checks.claim: Finite monomial decomposition, almost orthogonality and no cancellation.
check: For fixed l, only finitely many exponent tuples occur. The coefficient spaces are fixed finite-dimensional spaces, so constants depending on l are allowed.
After rescaling by |t|^(-sum l_i y_i), the diagonal norms are bounded above and below by fixed coefficient norms. The product splitting uses the fixed-width annulus in logarithmic coordinates.
A monomial has torus character (l1-l0,...,lm-l0). If two such characters agree, their exponent tuples differ by c(1,...,1). Since both tuples have minimum entry0, c=0; thus the tuples coincide.

All off-diagonal entries are O(C(l)|t|^epsilon) after this normalization. For fixed l,epsilon, choose t so that the finite Gram-matrix perturbation is smaller than half the diagonal coercivity. This proves the no-cancellation lower bound.
This check establishes why the min l_i=0 convention is essential and why there is no hidden monomial resonance in the stated decomposition.
preserved_checks.dependency: Existence and uniqueness of decomposition(28), and the restriction isomorphisms defining V_k, rely on earlier algebraic results not re-proved in this auxiliary segment.

preserved_checks.claim: Global pointwise bound(30), with a monomial exponent depending on z but not on y.
check: Use the weighted integral restricted to U_{y,t}; the generic-region upper bounds on phi_t and psi_t yield the needed lower bound there.
The OT upper bound and no-cancellation estimate bound every coefficient after its |t|^{sum l_i y_i} weight.

The point normalization |s(z)|=1 and triangle inequality select one coefficient tuple using only z and the fixed section s. Consequently that tuple does not depend on y, which is necessary for the later optimization over y.
The residual C(l)/|log|t|| is absorbed into C/l by choosing t sufficiently small after l is fixed. No uniform growth bound on C(l) is needed.
preserved_checks.excluded_artifact: The first intermediate lower bound printed on p.490 uses an unweighted integral over X_t despite deriving its weight bound only on U_{y,t}. The final displayed bound with U_{y,t} follows directly by first restricting the original weighted integral to U_{y,t}; this supplies the needed inequality without the stronger intermediate expression. This is recorded as an apparent integration-domain slip, not a retained substantive finding.

complete_check: For the selected exponent tuple, p=(-l0/l,...,-lm/l) belongs to Delta^vee by min l_i=0 and sum d_i l_i<=l.
Because u is Lipschitz and Delta^vee is bounded, shrinking Delta by epsilon changes sup_y(<p,y>-u(y)) by at most C epsilon, uniformly for p in Delta^vee.
Optimize inequality(30) over y, using the same tuple for every y. This gives psi_t(z)<=-u(x)-u*(p)+<p,x>+C/l+C epsilon.
The defining Legendre extension u(x)=max_{q in Delta^vee}(<q,x>-u*(q)) bounds the first three terms by0. This step does not require the actual x(z) to lie in the simplex.
Together with psi_t>=0, one obtains 0<=psi_t(z)<=C/l+C epsilon uniformly over all z, for t sufficiently small depending on l and epsilon.

Given a target eta>0, first choose epsilon with C epsilon<eta/2, then an integer l large enough that C/l<eta/2, then t below the corresponding threshold. This proves uniform convergence and involves no illicit exchange of l->infinity with t->0.

checks.question: Does C-infinity approximation on a high-measure smooth compact set, with equal total mass, suffice for the regularized stability application?
checks.result: Yes for the asymptotic application used in Corollary 6.4, under the regularization existence/local-approximation properties asserted in Remark 5.8. This check does not establish its stronger fixed-t arbitrary-TV approximation assertion.
assumptions: Fix t != 0 in the smooth family; write V=(L^n), mu=V mu_t, nu=omega_t^n. All are positive finite measures and nu(X_t)=mu(X_t)=V.

For any prescribed small eta>0, the good-region comparison in Proposition 5.6 allows t sufficiently small and a compact K in the smooth good region with mu(X_t\K)<=eta V and integral_K |nu-mu|<=eta V. Passing from an open good region to compact K costs an arbitrarily small mass, by inner regularity.

A smooth Kahler regularization omega_t,j is in the same cohomology class, tends locally smoothly to omega_t near K, and has arbitrarily small C0 potential difference, as asserted in Remark 5.8. The existence of this regularization is treated as a stated analytic dependency, not independently reproved here.
Local smooth convergence can be chosen after t and K are fixed, so integral_K |nu_j-nu|<=eta V where nu_j=omega_t,j^n. Its total mass is V by the common cohomology class.
complete_measure_estimate: Set a=integral_K |nu_j-mu|. The two local errors imply a<=2 eta V.
Equal total masses and positivity give nu_j(K^c)=V-nu_j(K)<=V-mu(K)+a=mu(K^c)+a.
Using the paper's integral absolute-difference convention for total variation, ||nu_j-mu||_TV <= a+nu_j(K^c)+mu(K^c) <= 2a+2mu(K^c) <= 6 eta V.

Thus for every prescribed stability tolerance gamma^(2n+3), first choose eta<gamma^(2n+3)/6, then t sufficiently small, then a sufficiently fine regularization for that t. No uniform smoothing scale or unjustified C0-to-TV continuity is required.
complete_stability_perturbation: Let lambda=|log|t|| and omega=omega_CY,t/lambda. If phi_t,j regularizes the ansatz potential phi_t, the smooth omega-psh function to use is q_j=-psi_t+(phi_t,j-phi_t)/lambda; then omega+dd^c q_j=omega_t,j/lambda.
From min psi_t=0, sup(-psi_t)=0. Choose ||q_j+psi_t||_C0<delta/8, so sup q_j>=-delta/8.
If the contrary hypothesis of Corollary 6.4 holds, mu_t({psi_t>delta})>delta. On that set q_j<-7delta/8, so the mass condition for Theorem 6.3 holds with a=-delta/2 and b=delta.
The uniform C0 bound is retained with one harmless fixed margin. The uniform Skoda estimate and its change of reference potential remain the paper's Theorems 6.1-6.2 dependencies.

Choose gamma below the theorem's allowed threshold and with C gamma<delta/8, then choose t and the regularization as above. Theorem 6.3 yields sup q_j<=-3delta/8, contradicting sup q_j>=-delta/8. The limiting weak estimate follows.
counterevidence_and_limits: C0 closeness of arbitrary potentials alone does not imply TV closeness of their Monge-Ampere measures; that inference is not used in the estimate above.

The proof above controls the regularized measure relative to V mu_t as t tends to zero. It does not by itself prove arbitrarily small TV distance to omega_t^n for every fixed t, which is stronger language in Remark 5.8.
No counterexample to that stronger fixed-t statement was constructed, and no Major finding is inferred from its not being independently established here.
The cited Skoda/capacity stability theorem and global regularization existence were not fetched or independently reproved; their stated hypotheses and the exact application were tracked.
